[ASSISTANT_SAID] Cilantro (Coriandrum sativum) is an annual herb that typically doesn't produce "babies" or offspring like some other plants do.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips to revive a wilting cilantro plant include checking soil moisture, adjusting the watering schedule, providing sufficient light, maintaining a comfortable temperature, fertilizing, pruning, and watching for pests.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For reviving cilantro, check soil moisture by sticking a finger into the soil; if it feels dry, it's time to water.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Cilantro needs consistent moisture, especially in hot or low humidity conditions; water when the top inch of soil feels dry.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Cilantro prefers full sun to partial shade; if it's not getting enough light, it may become leggy or wilted.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Cilantro prefers temperatures between 65°F (18°C) and 75°F (24°C).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Feed cilantro with a balanced, water-soluble fertilizer (5-5-5 NPK) once a month, diluted to half strength.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Pinch off wilted or damaged leaves to prevent disease and encourage bushy growth.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Check for pests like spider mites, aphids, or whiteflies and treat with insecticidal soap or neem oil.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To grow new cilantro plants, sow seeds every 1-2 weeks in well-draining potting mix, keeping the soil consistently moist and warm (70°F to 80°F or 21°C to 27°C) until germination (7-10 days).

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Fertilizing herbs is important for providing essential nutrients, promoting growth, and maintaining soil health.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] There are two main types of fertilizers: synthetic (quick, concentrated doses) and organic (slow-release, promotes soil health).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Before fertilizing, consider getting a soil test to determine pH and nutrient content.
